data.title: Flash sessions: --flash PROFILE at creation, the unlock-cycle hint, and flash in sav
data.description:
Why: the flash-chip model (gbcli-flash, e9cba4f) is reachable only from Rust (CoreConfig::flash). An agent building a GB Studio batteryless game, or any flash-save cart, cannot model its save from the CLI or protocol.

RULINGS (Ben, 2026-11-07; recorded in project/2026-11-07-flash-model.md, "Decided"):
- `--flash PROFILE` at session creation, like --model/--seed: named profiles only (no parameter overrides), stored in the bundle meta and as an optional checkpoint-header field (the profile name), checked on restore like the model (a conflict is bad_request), kept by power-cycle.
- A hint on sessions without a board: when a run sees a write that is an unlock cycle for some board, warn and name the flag with a matching profile.
- On a flash session, `sav` and `power-cycle --sav` export and import the flash save area as well as SRAM.
- Flash notes surface on the run that took them as warning rows and --json fields.
- The server's rebuild path (power_cycle across a rebuilt ROM) carries the flash contents as it carries the battery.

Wait for the independent review of e9cba4f (FFI, unsafe, blob format 4) before building on it; fix its findings first.

criteria.label: a session created with --flash runs, checkpoints, restores and power-cycles on that board (tests)
restore across boards is bad_request; a mask-ROM session that sends unlock cycles warns with the flag

data.title: Flash review fixes: mapper chosen from the padded size, command-address mask, notes lost on a refused load
data.description:
Findings from the review of e9cba4f, each with its probe in L00RuF-review_probes_flash.rs (run: cargo test -p gbcli-sameboy --test review_probes_flash -- --nocapture; four fail on purpose).

1. Low-medium. Padding the ROM to the chip size changes which mapper SameBoy picks. crates/sameboy/src/lib.rs:69-87 pads before GB_load_rom_from_buffer, and GB_configure_cart (crates/sameboy-sys/SameBoy/Core/mbc.c:190, :262) reads the padded size: (a) an MBC3 image on a board over 2 MiB (mx29lv320et, 4 MiB) becomes MBC30, widening the bank register to 8 bits (probe_mbc3_on_a_4mib_board_becomes_mbc30: "$2000<-$81: mask-ROM bank 1, flash bank 129"); (b) a ROM-only image ($0147=$00) padded past 32 KiB is treated as MBC3 (probe_rom_only_on_a_board_gains_an_mbc). The mapper type must come from the image's header, as on a mask-ROM session; only reach must grow.

2. Low; hardware half SUSPECTED. profiles.rs:166 sets command_mask 0x7FFF and profile.rs:133 compares bank*$4000+offset under it, so $4AAA/$4555 unlock cycles in the $4000 window match only on banks of one parity (probe_unlock_in_the_4000_window_depends_on_bank_parity: [(1,false,1),(2,true,0),(3,false,1),(4,true,0)] on generic-wr-aaa-aa). The reviewer recalls AMD 29LV160-class datasheets treating A11 and up as don't-care for command cycles; SST39SF040 decodes 15 bits. Check the datasheets (cite them) and set each profile's mask from its chip family.

3. Low. A load SameBoy refuses drops the chip's pending notes: the flash section loads first (lib.rs:648), FlashChip::load calls take_notes (state.rs:60), and the rollback at lib.rs:653 restores array and mode but not the notes (probe_a_refused_load_drops_pending_notes). A refused load must leave the core exactly as it was.

criteria.label: an MBC3 image on a 4 MiB board and a ROM-only image on any board keep their header's mapper (tests from the probes)
each profile's command-address mask is sourced from its chip's datasheet, and the 4000-window probe passes or is documented
a refused load leaves pending notes in place (test)

data.title: Joint conversion: per-target tiles behind one map and frame list
data.description:
Why: separate tile data per target keeps Ben's shade ruling inside tiles; a shared map keeps the program simple (plan question 1). What:

- The limits bg_tiles_map, vram_tiles and obj_tiles count joint tiles.
- Tiles-only images (assets/tiles/) are deduplicated the same way, with no map; their source tile -> index map is the result.
- Results fill the protocol types from leaf types.

data.title: Dual-mode starter: detect GBC, load palettes and the attribute map
data.description:
What: the starter (crates/build/templates/main.asm) does the following.
- It saves `a == BOOTUP_A_CGB` to an HRAM flag at Start, before `ldh a,[rLY]` overwrites A (lines 19-30).
- On a GBC, with the LCD off, it loads the BG and OBJ palettes through BCPS/BCPD and OCPS/OCPD with autoincrement.
- It writes the attribute map with VBK=1, then sets VBK back to 0.
- It copies the GBC tiles.

The DMG path must not touch VBK. A DMG has no VBK, so the attribute writes would overwrite the tilemap. Decide whether `new --gbc` or `build --gbc` brings the color path into the starter, and say which in the report.

data.text:
Fixed all three (worktree agent-aa1f8fbf7107e325f, uncommitted).
1. Mapper: SameBoy loads the unpadded image (mapper chosen as on mask ROM), then shim gbcli_set_rom_size grows the buffer to the chip ($FF) without GB_configure_cart. ROM-only on a board reaches 32 KiB (no bank register; hardware has 15 CPU address lines). MMM01 on a board refused; non-power-of-two chip size refused. No SameBoy patch.
2. Masks from datasheets: AAA boards/29dl163bd/am29lv160db $FFF (S29AL016D Table 10.1 n5, MX29LV160 PM0866 Table 5 n3, Am29DL16xD 21533 Table 14 n5), 555 boards $7FF (wiring inferred), mx29lv320et $FFF (inferred: PM1575 has no don't-care note), SST39SF040 $7FFF (DS20005022F Table 4-2 n1). Am29LV160D pub 22358 itself unreachable. Parity probe now passes.
3. FlashChip::load split into check_load/finish_load; SameBoy::load finishes the chip only after SameBoy accepts. No rollback.
Docs: project/2026-11-07-flash-model.md "Review fixes"; design §6 correction.

Built (worktree agent-aef9406a4e217d259, uncommitted). `gbcli build --gbc` -> wire `"target":"gbc"` in BuildArgs (typed enum `BuildTarget { Dmg, Gbc }` in crates/protocol/src/toolchain.rs, left off the wire when dmg so old request lines are unchanged). rgbfix gets `-c` for Gbc (project.rs), the failure remedy's "again" command carries `--gbc`, and `BuildMade.target` is always serialized (`"target":"dmg"` now appears in every build result, and the `build` row gains `target=`): the rgbds.txt golden changed for that reason only. Help: `gbcli help rgbds` maps GBC to Pan Docs' CGB and rgbfix -c/-C; the help golden now pins `help rgbds` and `build --help`. Schema lists `target?: "dmg"|"gbc"`.
Tests: build.rs (header $80 vs $00, checksum, result target; failed GBC build's remedy says --gbc), toolchain.rs serde test, topics.rs needle test, rgbds.rs CLI==serve for --gbc and the golden.

Differential test landed in the worktree (uncommitted): crates/engine/tests/opcode_rgbasm_differential.rs, generator crates/engine/tests/rgbasm/grammar.rs, shared rgbasm batch crates/engine/tests/rgbasm/mod.rs (spellings and probes now use it; their per-line helpers are gone).

Batch shape: one main.asm INCLUDEs l<i>.asm per line, each in a 4-byte slot at a fixed ROM0 address (Top: label, line, REDEF LEN EQU @-Top, ds 3-LEN, db LEN, PURGE Top). Own file per line isolates unterminated strings/block comments/trailing backslash; rgbasm names the included file in every diagnostic. rgbasm makes no object if anything fails, so rerun without the failing lines until it links: 2 rgbasm + 1 rgblink per batch of up to 4096 lines. rgbasm takes one input file, so "one file per line in a single invocation" means INCLUDE.

Found and fixed (CASES rows red first): LOW(bc) taken as condition c; ++ read as two pluses (it's string concat); mnemonic ended only at whitespace (rl[hl], set!$6,e); graphics constants >8 pixels refused (rgbasm warns); ldi/ldd refused HIGH(af); negated conditions (!nz) refused; `.` refused as a symbol; rgbasm folds x&&0, x||nonzero, x&0 to constants (bit wBar && 0, a assembles).

Set aside by rgbasm's own error (documented, counted per sweep): undefined symbol/section, jr out of reach, symbol in ldh address out of range, wrong-kind function argument (BANK(-Top)), interpolation, trailing backslash (line continuation), mnemonic alone listing forms.

Timing (load avg 6-10): warm 400 lines 0.20 s; pre-release 40,000 lines (10 seeds) 5.8 s. Exploratory 120k sweeps (seeds 100-129, 200-229) clean after fixes. Red demo: disabling the glued &/% number-prefix rule fails the warm test with 2 lines.

Built (uncommitted, worktree agent-aef9406a4e217d259). The seam LoadHigh imports:
- crates/protocol/src/palettes.rs (new): `Rgb555` newtype (the BCPD/OCPD word; JSON is the integer 0-32767, bit 15 refused; `from_rgb888` keeps each channel's top 5 bits as rgbgfx and census::key do, so a palette entry and a pixel of one #rrggbb are one color; `to_rgb888` is SameBoy's (x<<3)|(x>>2) for previews), `GbcPalette([Rgb555; 4])` (transparent), `NamedPalette { name, colors }`, `NamedPalettes { dmg: Option<GbcPalette>, palettes: Vec<NamedPalette> (file order = index), assignments: BTreeMap<image path under assets/, name> }` with deny_unknown_fields. `dmg` is a typed field, not a palette named "dmg": it's not a GBC palette and can't be assigned.
- crates/protocol/src/images.rs: `ImageKind::Tiles` ("tiles"); `ImageLimit::{GbcPalettes, GbcTileColors, DmgOverrideSize}`; `ImageAsset.tile_indices: Vec<Option<u32>>` (per 8x8 tile / 8x16 unit, row-major; null = transparent unit; target-independent, since tiles dedup on the (DMG, GBC) pair) and `ImageAsset.gbc: Option<GbcImage>`; `GbcImage { art: ImageArt (flattened: "art":"color" | "art":"indexed","palette":NAME), palettes: Vec<GbcPalette> (bg/tileset slot order; empty for sheets), tile_palettes: Vec<Option<u8>> parallel to tile_indices }`; `ImagesMade.gbc: Option<GbcImagesMade { obj_palettes }>`. All new fields skip when empty, so DMG JSON is unchanged: a new CLI golden `crates/gbcli/tests/cli/golden/images.json.txt` (blessed before the type change) pins a whole DMG build line.
- Target per image is implicit: every image has a DMG version; `gbc` is present exactly when the target is GBC. No per-image target list.
- `gbcli schema` lists the types with two examples a test parses into them.
- `ImageKind::Tiles` arms in crates/build are `unreachable!` (find never yields a tileset until the joint leaf).

data.text:
Built (worktree agent-aa1f8fbf7107e325f, uncommitted). As in design §6 update "flash sessions, as ruled".
- --flash BOARD (named only) -> RomSource/SessionFile.flash; unknown = bad_request listing boards; differing on reopen = SettingDiffers. Boot cache key gains -<board>.
- CheckpointHeader.flash (optional, absent = mask ROM; old files load unchanged). Restore: FlashConflict bad_request after the model step.
- Machine::power_cycle(battery, Flash::Keep|Carried|Image, rtc). Server rebuild path carries head flash_contents (changed sectors only).
- File shape chosen: sav PATH also writes PATH-with-ext-.flash.gb (game.sav -> game.flash.gb), raw whole chip image. Why: .sav stays SameBoy's; the image is a flasher's ROM backup, diffable, and runs in any emulator with the save in it. Import = sectors differing from ROM on disk (warn if inside the image extent). Either file may be missing.
- Run: notes -> warnings + result.flash_notes rows (ticks addr value kind board? text).
- Mask-ROM hint: SameBoy UnlockWatch on every mask-ROM core (write callback always installed there), first named WR board's unlock cycle per take -> NoChip note; warning names --flash <board>.
- help flash topic, schema, --help, goldens flash.txt/help.txt. Test ROM crates/engine/tests/roms/flash_save.asm (built with rgbasm/rgblink/rgbfix -v -p 0, as build-roms.sh does).

Built (uncommitted, worktree agent-aef9406a4e217d259). crates/build/src/images/palettes.rs replaces palette.rs (git rm'd). Grammar: `name: c0 c1 c2 c3` (#rrggbb or #rgb, kept as RGB555 via Rgb555::from_rgb888, top 5 bits), `path = name` (path under assets/); `#` as a word of its own starts a comment anywhere, any other `#` word is a color, so a fifth color is an error (the d0e891a review case). Names: [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. palette_file with line for: neither form, != 4 colors, bad color, bad name, duplicate name (dmg too), duplicate assignment, unknown palette (lists the defined ones), dmg assigned, image not in the project (lists its images; checked with no images too). count/max = colors read vs 4 on palette lines, else 1/1. The dmg duplicate-in-RGB555 refusal kept; named palettes may repeat a color.
One behavior change, documented in design §12's new update: the declared rule's nearest entry is measured in RGB555 (keys) not 8-bit RGB, because entries arrive as Rgb555 (from the file or a client's NamedPalettes). #070707 beside #080808/#000000 entries now takes #000000's shade (it is #000000 to rgbgfx); new unit test, red under the old metric. Every earlier declared test case keeps its result.
Without --gbc: dmg drives the cascade, the rest is checked, assigned images build byte-identical DMG art (crates/build/tests/images_named_palettes.rs). Named palettes are not yet emitted (api leaf zcxvjc) and ImagesMade doesn't carry them.

data.description:
Found by the independent review of fc85d19 (6pr1FU, 4hM0UN), 2026-11-07; probes in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-gbcli/59babd94-818e-4007-b5ad-0f753af04730/scratchpad/fsess-engine-probes.rs (crates/engine/tests) and fsess-server-probes.rs (crates/server/tests); both fail today.

1. LOW. Flash notes and the mask-ROM hint from `step` land on the next run or are lost. Handler::step (crates/server/src/handle/run/mod.rs:340-391) never calls take_flash_notes; only run does (mod.rs:189-194). after_run_error (mod.rs:313) keeps the machine warm without taking notes too. Repro: cargo test -p gbcli-server --test review_probes_flash -- --nocapture: on generic-wr-aaa-aa 40 frame steps give no warnings and the next 1-frame run reports flash_notes [(11765560, 0x0AAA, DataLines)]; on mask ROM the --flash hint appears on the run after the steps. Help flash and design §6 say notes are on the run that took them. Fix: every op that advances the machine (step, run, run errors) reports its own notes.

2. LOW. Across a rebuild, Flash::Carried in Machine::power_cycle (crates/engine/src/machine/power.rs) adopts every changed 64 KiB sector, even where the new ROM's image now lies; flash_sectors_in_image and its warning run only for Flash::Image. Repro: cargo test -p gbcli-engine --test review_probes_flash probe_carried: flash_save.gb saves into bank 12, a rebuild grows to 256 KiB, chip[$30000]=0x42 (old save) over the new code, flash_sectors_in_image=0. Design §6 says "the new build's code stays". Integrator's ruling (two-way door): a carried sector that overlaps the new image's extent is not carried, and the rebuild warns naming the dropped sectors (the save no longer fits beside the code).

Nits: flash_tests.rs's an_image_of_the_wrong_size_is_refused_and_changes_nothing asserts only the message (assert the chip is unchanged); help flash's "commands at $4AAA/$4555" line suggests am29lv160db is the only fit though $FFF decoding makes it read as $0AAA (say so); sav writes game.flash.gb before game.sav, leaving the first if the second fails (write both or neither).

criteria.label: a step, and a run that errors, report the notes and hint they took (tests from the probes)
a rebuild that grows into a carried sector keeps the new code and warns naming the sector (test from the probe)
the three nits are fixed

data.text:
Review of 54c9d3e (packing; twelfth session, reviewer given the code): nothing serious. Settles this leaf's open note, tested against rgbgfx 1.0.4 -c (script: scratchpad gbcp-rgbgfx.py, under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-gbcli/9231daa0-c167-47d3-9376-bfb7093f074b/scratchpad/):
1. MEDIUM, for this leaf: an OBJ spec written as pack.rs lays the palette out (#ffffff in slot 0) is REJECTED by rgbgfx -c for any image with an alpha-0 pixel ("Each palette spec can only contain up to 3 colors plus the implict transparent color"). Write slot 0 as #none in the -c spec: `#none,#ffffff,#ff0000,#000000` maps clear->0, white->1, red->2, black->3; padded `#none,#ff0000,#ff0000,#ff0000` also works. Keep the palette-RAM form (GbcPalette, white in slot 0 is harmless there) separate from the rgbgfx-spec form, e.g. a spec renderer keyed on Layer; fix pack.rs's "index 0 holds white" doc so it doesn't read as rgbgfx-ready.
   BG padding with the darkest color is ACCEPTED: duplicates in a spec are fine, a pixel takes the first matching slot; RGB555 truncation agrees with rgbgfx (0x0F0000 matches #080000).
2. LOW: pack's census drops only alpha-0 pixels (alpha 1-254 counts as opaque; alpha 0 in a BG is silently skipped). Safe only because census::alpha (bg.rs:52 strict, sheet.rs:87) rejects those first. Run census::alpha before pack in the wiring and pin it with a test.
3. NIT: a gbc_palettes message lists every cell past the budget (~995 tiles on a 32x32 random background). Cap the message list with "... and N more", keep every tile in `tiles`.
4. NIT: ImageLimit::GbcPalettes `count` doc says "the lower bound or the palettes placed, whichever is larger"; it is always placed+reserved (placed >= bound). Say that.
Checked sound: 3000 random BG and OBJ cases (every success valid, every failure true by exhaustive minimum), hidden exact partitions found, 1024-tile overflow search 78 ms, determinism (no HashMap; fixed u32 step bound), cell coordinates, bound validity, gbc model alias (resolved to the enum before the session guard). Probes kept at scratchpad gbcp_probes.rs (a #[cfg(test)] mod under crates/build/src/images/pack/).

From tzEhz3 (3b72e81), for this leaf: (1) images::convert now takes BuildTarget; per image a Version {Art, Derived, Override(Pixels)} decides the DMG version; the derived/override pixels go to rgbgfx via the .merged.png transient. The COLOR pixels are in hand in convert's loop but dropped after derive: this leaf must keep them alongside the DMG version to pair (DMG tile, GBC tile). (2) images/mod.rs is now 522 lines, past the ~400 ceiling: move the per-image version choice into derive.rs (or a new module) as part of reworking this loop. (3) Derived vs overridden isn't on the wire; if LoadHigh or the assets op needs it, it belongs on ImageArt::Color in crates/protocol/src/images/gbc.rs.

data.description:

Probes: scratchpad gbct_probes_protocol.rs (for crates/protocol/tests) and gbct_probes_build.rs (crates/build/tests) under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-gbcli/9231daa0-c167-47d3-9376-bfb7093f074b/scratchpad/; each probe PASSES today, confirming its finding (invert it for the red test).

LoadHigh asks for (index, flip) (note on 7gGMeZ). 4. LOW. GbcImage.tile_palettes isn't tied to tile_indices: length, None positions, slot 0-7 unchecked (probe gbct_parallel_lengths_and_slot_range_are_unenforced). Fix with 1: make the invariant unrepresentable or validated.

6. LOW. An old assets/palette.txt is silently ignored (probe gbct_old_palette_txt_is_silently_ignored): warn naming palettes.txt.
Nits: census::key (census.rs:15) and Rgb555::from_rgb888 truncate separately: one should call the other; schema example's dmg entry 21140 isn't #aaaaaa (22197); check_images reports missing images alphabetically, not in file order (palettes.rs:313).

data.title: Warm suite back under 30 s: one test binary per crate, fewer warm song samples, shorter waits
data.description:
Why: the warm suite is over its 30 s budget. scripts/bench/test-times.py, twelfth session (load 11.5, reviewers compiling): 107 binaries, sum 57.8 s wall, 108 s CPU. The sixth session measured 48 binaries at 14.5 s on an idle machine.

Where it goes:
- ~75 binaries finish in under 0.3 s, ~0.09 s of it process start: about 9 s of overhead, and a link step for each binary.
- gbcli-build::music_equiv: 8.0 s wall, 31.6 s CPU. It has 15 sample tests at 600 frames, about 1.3 s each, ~90% of it emulation (Frames(1) takes 0.3 s). The frames include the ~150-frame boot. Every sample's whole song is already in the pre-release suite.
- 0.1.0::cli errors::session_busy_says_to_wait: 5.05 s wall, 0.04 s CPU. It waits out LOCK_WAIT (crates/bundle/src/lock.rs:14, 5 s).
- gbcli-build::build_safety: 4 s wall, 1.3 s CPU. Its hang and child-process tests wait on timeouts (3.08 s, 1.66 s, 1.51 s).
- gbcli-build::images_bg: a test at 2.2 s wall and 0.1 s CPU.
- gbcli-build toolchain tests: 0.5-0.9 s wall at 0.02 s CPU.

What: one integration-test binary per crate where tests can share a process; fewer warm music samples, and no boot frames in the warm comparison; shorter waits where the test proves the same thing. Record the figures in an update to project/2026-11-06-test-suite-speed.md.

criteria.label: test-times.py on a quiet machine sums under 30 s wall; the figures and the load are in the speed doc
no test is lost: every test in the old binaries runs in the new ones or the pre-release suite (count before and after)

data.title: Flash: a restore across a compatible rebuild drops saved sectors over the new code; sav's pair claim; schema nit
data.description:
Found by the independent verification of 6c5b029 (DkhKgi), twelfth session. Probes: scratchpad flfx_engine_probes.rs (crates/engine/tests) and flfx_server_probes.rs (crates/server/tests) under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-gbcli/9231daa0-c167-47d3-9376-bfb7093f074b/scratchpad/; the flfx_* probes FAIL today (they assert the fixed behavior).

1. MEDIUM. After a compatible rebuild (no live symbol moved), every op that loads the head (run, step, show, ...) goes through Machine::restore (crates/engine/src/machine.rs:330-387); step 7's core.load(&cp.blob) brings the checkpoint's changed flash sectors in through FlashChip::finish_load -> adopt, checked only against the chip's size, never against the new image's extent. The old save lands over the new build's code; the only warning is "the ROM changed but no live symbol moved". The next head is saved under the new ROM hash, so later power cycles use Flash::Keep and the 6c5b029 guard (contents_past, power.rs) never runs: permanent. Same with --allow-rom-change. Repro: cargo test -p gbcli-server --test flfx_server_probes flfx_ -- --nocapture (flash_save.gb, --flash generic-wr-aaa-a9, 200 frames, grow to 256 KiB, run 1 frame, sav: chip[$30000]=0x42, all 65536 bytes differ); cargo test -p gbcli-engine --test flfx_engine_probes flfx_.
Ruling (integrator, two-way door, same as DkhKgi's for power cycle): when a restore crosses a ROM change, changed flash sectors that overlap the new image are not adopted, and the restore warns naming the dropped sectors, as power cycle does. One rule, one code path for both crossings.
2. LOW. sav's write_all_atomically (crates/server/src/handle/shot.rs:765-795) renames game.sav then game.flash.gb; a kill between them leaves a new .sav beside an old .flash.gb (and a stray temp). Design §6's correction says "both or neither" unqualified. Fix: qualify the doc (and the function's doc comment) honestly, or make the pair detectable; integrator prefers the honest doc unless detection is cheap.
3. NIT. crates/cli/src/help/schema.rs:69-70: the error object lists "flash_notes"? but not "keys_unapplied"?, which ErrorBody carries.

criteria.label: a run, step or show after a compatible rebuild keeps the new code where the image lies, keeps sectors past it, and warns naming the dropped ones (tests from the probes)
power cycle and restore share one rule for carried sectors
sav's both-or-neither claim is true as written; the schema lists keys_unapplied

data.text:
From k5Kadv and jJjaK9 (agent gbc-types), what this leaf consumes. Branch worktree-agent-ab0520ba5526fec0e until merged.

Protocol shape changed (jJjaK9): ImageAsset.tile_indices and GbcImage.tile_palettes are gone. One ImageAsset.tile_map: Vec<Option<TileEntry>>, TileEntry { index: u32, flip: Flip (none|x|y|xy, oam_bits() = $20/$40), palette: Option<PaletteSlot> } (crates/protocol/src/images/map.rs). index = tile in the image's own data; a sheet unit's top tile (2*unit). On read (images/asset.rs) every entry must carry a slot exactly when the image has gbc, and only a sheet may flip or have a null entry: fill both together. GbcImage is now { art, palettes }.

Indexed art (k5Kadv), crates/build/src/images/indexed.rs, wired in images::convert (which now takes the BuildTarget):
- indexed::assigned(&NamedPalettes, path_under_assets) -> Option<&NamedPalette>: an assigned image is indexed.
- indexed::ObjSlots::new(&named, &sheet_paths): distinct palettes assigned to sheets, in NamedPalettes::palettes order, take OBJ slots 0..n. slot(name), colors() (the start of obj_palettes), reserved() (= n: pass it as pack(..., Layer::Obj, reserved)), problem() (gbc_palettes when n > 8).
- indexed::background(palette, &tilemap_bytes) / indexed::sheet(palette, &SheetPlan, slot) -> (GbcImage, tile_map). Background: BG slot 0, palettes [its colors]. Sheet: SheetPlan::tile_map(slot) from the new SheetPlan.units (each sheet unit -> (kept unit, Flip)).
- convert under --gbc sets asset.gbc + asset.tile_map for indexed images only, and made.gbc = GbcImagesMade { obj_palettes: ObjSlots::colors() }. Color images get gbc: None and an empty tile_map until this leaf.

Decision you inherit (deviation from GbcImagesMade's old doc, which said packed first): assigned palettes take the FIRST OBJ slots, packed color-sheet palettes follow. pack() now numbers its slots from `reserved` (Packing::first_slot; cell_palettes are Vec<Vec<Option<PaletteSlot>>>), so pack(sources, Obj, obj_slots.reserved()) gives the color sheets' slots directly, and obj_palettes = obj_slots.colors() followed by packing.palettes. Why: a swap program's slots for its named palettes don't move when color art changes. Packing::gbc_image(layer) no longer takes a source index; the slots are in cell_palettes, to go into each TileEntry.

Indexed art's joint dedup is its DMG dedup (GBC tile = DMG tile), so you can keep its tile_map as is; for a sheet keep the flip dedup (the plan's line 68 is corrected: sheets already dedup with flips). Its frame-list attribute bytes (api leaf) take the slot from TileEntry.palette.

Roster (twelfth session): gbc-types -> Aifjyb (was jJjaK9) then k5Kadv; gbc-derive -> tzEhz3 (done, 3b72e81). suite-speed -> 9RaRvi (was XeGILY), all crates tests/ layout: integrate first among the rest, then carry the others' new test files into its layout. flash-restore -> ahKOkk (was g83MoZ). The leaf ids changed because .jobs/log was reverted by a git reset in the main checkout and the leaves were recreated.

(Recreated from the agent flash-restore's note on g83MoZ, lost to a log reset:)
flash-restore: one rule for both crossings is now a chip method, FlashChip::revert_overlapping(end, rom) (Core::revert_flash_overlapping; engine helper keep_the_image_code), applied after the state is taken over: by Machine::restore when the ROM hash changed, and by power_cycle(Flash::Carried). gbcli_flash::contents_past is removed. Restore warns LoadWarning::FlashSectorsDropped; the text lives in StoreError::warning_text and power-cycle uses it too. Seam note: the server's power cycle across a rebuild restores the head (forced) into a scratch machine built from the new ROM, so with this fix the sectors are dropped by that restore, not by power_cycle; the handler now forwards that restore's FlashSectorsDropped warning (it discarded the restore's warnings before), or the power-cycle warning would have vanished. sav: doc qualified (a kill between the renames leaves a mismatched pair); no detection.

Fixed on branch worktree-agent-ab0520ba5526fec0e (agent gbc-types), uncommitted for the integrator.
1. ImageAsset.tile_indices + GbcImage.tile_palettes -> ImageAsset.tile_map: Vec<Option<TileEntry { index, flip: Flip, palette: Option<PaletteSlot> }>> (protocol images/map.rs). Field renamed (tile_map), since it no longer holds bare indices. Index doc pins: tile in the image's own data, a sheet unit's top tile (even). Sheet's Object.flip is now the protocol Flip, so emit's $20/$40 come from Flip::oam_bits. Plan line 68 corrected in place (block quote).
2. NamedPalettes: protocol palettes/rules.rs (faults/check, serde try_from). File parser calls faults() and reports the earliest line. Path rule: <bg|sprites|tiles>/<file>.png only.
3. BuildMade.target #[serde(default)].
4. Unrepresentable: the slot rides in each entry (no parallel array); PaletteSlot is 0-7 by type; ImageAsset's try_from checks slot presence == gbc presence and flip/null only in sheets.
5. (No fix: GbcImage stays output-only.)
6. Old assets/palette.txt -> palette_file warning naming assets/palettes.txt (with or without images; Converted gained an explicit `stopped` so a warning-only no-image result doesn't fail the build).
Nits: census::key calls Rgb555::from_rgb888; schema dmg example 22197; check_images in file order.

Update to my 19:27 note (gbc-types), after rebasing onto 3b72e81 (tzEhz3): the leaf named there as jJjaK9 is Aifjyb. Everything in that note still holds, with one change in shape: images::convert now builds an `indexed::Indexed` (named palettes + ObjSlots) under --gbc and calls `fill_background(path, &tilemap, &mut asset)` / `fill_sheet(path, &plan, &mut asset)` and `made()` (the GbcImagesMade); ObjSlots (reserved(), slot(), colors()) and the free functions assigned/background/sheet are unchanged beneath it. tzEhz3's `Version` enum and its choice moved into derive.rs (`derive::version`, behavior unchanged): indexed art under --gbc is Version::Art, and a .dmg.png beside indexed art is a layout error. images/mod.rs is 524 lines (main had 522); when the joint conversion reworks the loop, the per-image rgbgfx/preview arm is the next thing to move out.

(1) ObjSlots is keyed by (palette, OBP): palettes in file order, each palette's OBPs ascending by value; a slot's colors are by_obp(named, obp), entry i = named[(obp >> 2i) & 3] (entry 0 = shade 0's, never drawn). reserved() = slot count; >8 is gbc_palettes, message lists "name by OBP %bbbbbbbb". (3) ImageAsset read check: map length = width*height (sheet: width*height/2), empty only without gbc, index < tiles, sheet index even with index+1 < tiles; every_built_result_round_trips (DMG and GBC) guards it. From BiIfeX (review finding 5, confirmed real by reading, not built): nothing checks that a sheet's .dmg.png override is transparent exactly where its color image is. derive::override_size checks only the size; sheet::check then runs on the override's pixels, so the kept units, the frame lists (which objects exist) and the transparent units of tile_map all follow the override's alpha. If the joint conversion draws the color image's tiles through that one frame list, a unit opaque in color but transparent in the override gets no object and never draws on the GBC, and pixels opaque in the override but clear in color draw as color index 0 (transparent), silently. Unit dedup is keyed on the DMG data too, so two color units that differ but share DMG data would collapse. Suggested check for this leaf: per pixel, alpha of the override == alpha of the color image (an error naming the tiles, like dmg_override_size), plus the dedup key over both versions. Backgrounds have no transparency (census::alpha refuses it), so only sheets are affected.

Correction to my previous note: "Backgrounds have no transparency (census::alpha refuses it), so only sheets are affected" was wrong. census::alpha runs only in bg::check and sheet::check, on the DMG version. With a .dmg.png override, the DMG version is the override, so a color background's own transparent or half-transparent pixels are never checked (the derived path is fine: derive keeps transparency, and bg::check refuses it). So the alpha-agreement check belongs to both kinds: for a background, the color image must be fully opaque; for a sheet, its alpha must match the override's pixel for pixel.

data.title: Decide: indexed sheets' colors shift when color art is added without a dmg line
data.description:
Found by the independent review of 2efed71 (thirteenth session, reviewer review-wire13, given the code). Confirmed by probe: scratchpad/probes/build_review_wire13_probe.rs under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ben-git-gbcli/d63f3736-338a-40eb-9536-20d0f5e87808/ (goes in crates/build/tests/it with a mod line).

With no `dmg` line in assets/palettes.txt, the shade cascade stretches shades over every color in the project (crates/build/src/images/shades.rs:3-11; sheet.rs:137). Adding an unrelated color-art sheet therefore changes an indexed sheet's OBP and, through Ben's reorder-by-OBP ruling, the contents of its OBJ palette slot: in the probe, the hero's slot goes from [e0,e0,e3,e0] to [e0,e1,e2,e0] when a white/black/red color sheet is added. If one palette's two OBPs swap order under the stretch, slot numbering moves too (not built). Both follow from two rulings together (one color one shade everywhere; reorder by OBP), so this is not a coding mistake. The DMG look of the indexed sheet changes too, consistently.

Options:
(a) Warn under --gbc when indexed art exists and palettes.txt has no dmg line; remedy: add a dmg line so indexed art's shades are pinned. (Recommended: it keeps today's behavior, costs one warning, and is reversible.)
(b) Refuse that case (an error naming the dmg line).
(c) Leave it; document that color art can recolor indexed sheets when no dmg line is set.

data.title: Name the manifest's palettes.dmg field, not assets/palettes.txt, in image remedies for a manifest
data.description:
Why: found by the independent review of 4381e6a (fourteenth session, reviewer review14). When images are converted from a manifest (`gbcli assets --manifest`), remedies tell the author to edit the wrong thing.

What: every image remedy that points at the dmg setting names it as the palettes source actually is. For a project that's "the dmg line of assets/palettes.txt"; for a manifest it's the JSON field `palettes.dmg` (four RGB555 colors, shades 0-3), and "gbcli help images" doesn't document that field. Cases:
- `shades_unpinned` (crates/build/src/images/indexed.rs, fn unpinned): says "add a dmg line to the manifest's palettes"; there is no line in a manifest.
- `shade_stretched` (crates/build/src/images/shared.rs, fn stretched) and the shared-shade REMEDY constant (shared.rs top): hardcode assets/palettes.txt even for a manifest.
- the indexed-art-plus-.dmg.png error (crates/build/src/images/derive.rs, around line 75): says "assets/palettes.txt assigns it" for a manifest too.
- the doc comment on ImageLimit::ShadesUnpinned (crates/protocol/src/images.rs) names only assets/palettes.txt.
Reproduction: crates/gbcli/tests/cli/golden/assets.txt line 4 (a manifest under --gbc). `palette_shown` in pipeline.rs already knows the source ("the manifest's palettes" vs the palettes.txt path); thread a typed value for the source rather than comparing strings.

Out of scope: the `assets … warnings=0` toolchain-only count next to `images … warnings=1`, which is by design (reviewer finding 2); raise it at review-ab if the game agents trip on it.

data.title: PPU mode at raster writes: a spike, and the HBlank recipe
data.description:
Why: both example-game agents' costliest stumble (project/2026-11-08-examples-dx-review.md, item 1). `--raster` prints `into=` ticks then `raster_unsupported feature=ppu_mode_events`, so "every scroll write lands in HBlank" has no direct check. Both agents invented a conditional breakpoint on the write instruction (`gbcli break PC --if '([rSTAT] & 3) != 0'`), which caught two real late writes in the racer. On the racer that same condition failed the run with `unsupported (SideEffectFreeIo): PPU registers are unavailable while mode-3 cycles are batched`, while `show` reported a breakpoint stop: the exact case the check exists for, reported ambiguously.

What: (1) A recipe in `gbcli recipes` and a line in `gbcli help traps` for checking that a write lands in HBlank, whatever the spike finds. (2) A spike, answered in a dated finding: can the SameBoy adapter record the PPU mode (and the dot, if cheap) at each raster write, and can a condition read `[rSTAT]` without the batching refusal (for example by evaluating STAT from the adapter's own mode tracking, or by unbatching around breakpoints that have conditions)? If yes, implement `mode=` on `raster_write` and fix the condition so it either evaluates or refuses before it stops, never both. (3) Re-check the bespoke-core un-park condition (project/backlog.md, A bespoke Rust emulator core) against the result, and say in the finding whether it now holds.

Seams: crates/sameboy (the adapter, vendored SameBoy patches), crates/engine (raster observation, conditions), crates/protocol (RasterWrite), CLI render and help. The gotchas file explains the vendored-SameBoy patch workflow (scripts/vendor-sameboy.sh).

Out of scope: mid-mode-3 accuracy itself.

criteria.label: the HBlank recipe and traps line exist, with a test that the recipe's commands parse
a dated finding answers the spike's two questions with evidence, and says whether the bespoke-core un-park condition holds
if feasible, raster_write carries the mode (test against a ROM writing in HBlank and in mode 3), and a [rSTAT] condition never both errors and stops (regression test from the racer's case)

data.title: run's output: lcd_off in the frame budget, one-row key_unapplied, per-read errors, --dir anchoring
data.description:
Why: four run-output stumbles from the example games (project/2026-11-08-examples-dx-review.md, items 3, 4, 10, 12). Both agents wrote Python to filter the frame budget.

What:
- Frame budget: a per-frame `lcd_off` flag in `--json`; the summary row counts LCD-off frames apart from lag (e.g. `lag=0 lcd_off=7`) and leaves them out of `busiest`/`active_max`. The help topic `budgets` says so.
- key_unapplied: a stopped run with leftover key events prints one row (`keys_unapplied count=N first=KEY@FRAME`) instead of a warning listing them plus one row each; `--json` keeps the full list.
- An uninitialized `--read` (or any one failing read) reports that read's error in its row and keeps the stop and the other reads, rather than failing the run with exit 3 (`--allow-uninit` keeps its meaning for the values).
- `--dir` anchors relative paths given to the command (the ROM path at least), and `gbcli build DIR --session S` finds S under DIR.
- Docs: `gbcli recipes` gains the closed-loop input bot pattern both agents used (drive a session a few frames at a time with `--read`, record key changes, replay with `--keys-file`); the help says held keys persist across runs.

Seams: crates/engine (frame budget), crates/server (run handling), crates/cli (render, args, recipes, help), crates/protocol. Keep goldens honest.
